idiom_name: compose/pipe helpers built on rest parameters and Array.prototype.reduce
implementation_notes: JavaScript needs no library for the core of the pattern: functions are first-class, so a three-line `pipe`/`compose` (rest parameters plus `reduce`) replaces any class hierarchy of Strategy or Command objects, and `andThen` is literally `f` applied to the result of `g`. For asynchronous steps the same idea appears as promise chaining - MDN documents sequential composition as `funcs.reduce((p, f) => p.then(f), Promise.resolve())` and names the reusable version `composeAsync` - with `Promise.all`/`allSettled` as the fan-out combinators. Reach for a library when the DSL outgrows a handful of helpers.
pitfalls: Composition drops the receiver: `pipe(obj.method)` loses `this`, so bind the method or wrap it in a lambda.
An `orElse` implemented with try/catch swallows programmer errors together with expected failures; distinguish failure kinds explicitly instead of catching everything.
Promise combinators start work eagerly: `Promise.all([...])` launches every step immediately, so a combinator description is not lazy and cannot be re-run for a retry without rebuilding it.

variants.name: Ramda: curried, data-last combinator library
variants.idiom_name: R.pipe / R.compose with curried building blocks (R.map, R.filter, R.prop)
variants.implementation_notes: Ramda is the JavaScript ecosystem's combinator library in the catalog's sense: every function is automatically curried and data-last, `R.pipe`/`R.compose` build left-to-right/right-to-left pipelines, and point-free definitions are assembled from `R.map`, `R.filter`, `R.prop`, `R.reduce` instead of classes or methods. Choose it when a team wants a shared vocabulary rather than home-grown helpers; note that currying infers arity from the function's `length`, so variadic or optional-argument functions need an explicit `R.curryN`.
pitfalls: Auto-currying relies on arity: a variadic function reports `length === 0`, so pipelines silently compose the wrong thing unless `R.curryN` fixes the arity.
Point-free style hides data flow and types; a mis-ordered pipeline is only detected by a runtime TypeError deep inside the chain.
Bundling all of Ramda for a handful of helpers bloats the client bundle - use partial builds or prefer the native idiom.
